hook: There are three types of procrastination. Most advice only fixes one of them.
topic: The three types of procrastination — avoidance, ambiguity, perfectionism
body:
**There are three types of procrastination. Most advice only fixes one of them. That's why the advice keeps failing you.**

Type one: avoidance procrastination. You know what the task is, but the emotional weight attached to it — fear of failure, fear of judgment — makes starting feel dangerous. The fix here is emotional decoupling, not better scheduling.

Type two: ambiguity procrastination. You can't start because the task isn't clear enough to act on. "Work on the project" is not a task your brain can execute. It doesn't know what movement to make first. The fix is specificity — define the first physical action, not the goal.

Type three: perfectionism procrastination. You won't start until conditions are right — until you have the right time, the right energy, the right setup. The fix here is constraint — you have to artificially restrict the quality expectation to make a start possible.

The reframe: if you've been using the same productivity system for all three, you now know why it only works some of the time. You've been applying a single solution to three different problems.

One action: label the task you're currently avoiding — avoidance, ambiguity, or perfectionism. The label alone changes your response to it.

More on the full system in the link in bio.
